questions.q: The density $\rho$ of a uniform cylinder is determined by measuring its mass $m$, length $l$ and diameter $d$. The measured values of $m$, $l$ and $d$ are $97.42 \pm 0.02$ g, $8.35 \pm 0.05$ mm and $20.20 \pm 0.02$ mm, respectively. Calculated percentage fractional error in $\rho$ is _______.
questions.solution:
The density of a uniform cylinder is given by $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V} = \dfrac{4m}{\pi d^2 l}$

The percentage fractional error in density is given by:

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\dfrac{\Delta d}{d} + \dfrac{\Delta l}{l} \right) \times 100$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{0.02}{97.42} + 2 \times \dfrac{0.02}{20.20} + \dfrac{0.05}{8.35} \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = \left( 0.000205 + 0.00198 + 0.005988 \right) \times 100$

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = 0.008173 \times 100 = 0.8173\%$

Rounding off to two decimal places, the percentage error is $0.82\%$.

Answer: $0.82\%$

For parallel combination: $k_{eq} = k_1 + k_2 = 10 + 20 = 30$ N/m
For sum, absolute errors add:
$\Delta k_{eq} = \Delta k_1 + \Delta k_2 = 0.2 + 0.3 = 0.5$ N/m
Percentage error $= \frac{\Delta k_{eq}}{k_{eq}} \times 100 = \frac{0.5}{30} \times 100 = 1.67\%$

questions.q: The energy of a system is given as $\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{t})=\alpha^3 \mathrm{e}^{-\beta t}$, where t is the time and $\beta=0.3 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. The errors in the measurement of $\alpha$ and $t$ are $1.2 \%$ and $1.6 \%$, respectively. At $t=5 \mathrm{~s}$, maximum percentage error in the energy is :
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& d E=3 \alpha^2 d \alpha e^{-\beta t}+\alpha^3 e^{-\beta t}(-\beta) d t \\
& \frac{d E}{E}=\frac{3 d \alpha}{\alpha}+(-\beta) d t \\
& \frac{\Delta E}{E}=\frac{3 \Delta \alpha}{\alpha}+\beta \Delta t
\end{aligned}$
(\%) $\Delta t=1.6 \% \times 5=8 \% \%\left(\frac{3 \Delta \alpha}{\alpha}\right)=3 \times 1.2 \%=3.6 \%$
Putting values we get
$\Rightarrow 3.6+8 \times 0.3=6 \%$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}=\cos (\mathrm{kt}) \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\sin (\mathrm{kt}) \hat{\mathrm{j}} ;|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}|=1 \\ & \because \overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}=\mathrm{m} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}} \\ & \therefore \hat{\mathrm{P}}=\hat{\mathrm{v}} \\ & \Rightarrow \hat{\mathrm{v}}=\cos (\mathrm{kt}) \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\sin (\mathrm{kt}) \hat{\mathrm{j}} \\ & \hat{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{-\mathrm{k} \sin (\mathrm{kt}) \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{k} \cos (\mathrm{kt}) \hat{\mathrm{j}}}{\mathrm{k}} \\ & \Rightarrow \hat{\mathrm{a}}=-\sin k t \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\cos \mathrm{kt} \hat{\mathrm{j}} \\ & \because \hat{\mathrm{F}}=\hat{\mathrm{a}}=-\sin \mathrm{kt} \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\cos \mathrm{kt} \hat{\mathrm{j}} \\ & \cos \theta=\frac{\hat{\mathrm{F}} \cdot \hat{\mathrm{P}}}{|\hat{\mathrm{F}}||\hat{\mathrm{P}}|}=-\frac{\sin \mathrm{kt} \cos \mathrm{t}+\sin \mathrm{kt} \cos \mathrm{t}}{1 \times 1}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Rules for significant figures:

1. All non-zero numbers are significant

5. Trailing zeros in a whole number with the decimal shown are significant

(A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.q:
The radius $\left(r\right)$, length $\left(l\right)$ and resistance $\left(R\right)$ of a metal wire was measured in the laboratory as

$r = \left(0 .35 \pm 0 .05\right)cm$, $R = \left(100 \pm 10\right)ohm$, $l = \left(15 \pm 0 .2\right)cm$

The percentage error in resistivity of the material of the wire is :
questions.solution:
The resistance of the wire is given as, $R = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$

Therefore, $ρ = R\dfrac{A}{l}$

$ρ = R\dfrac{\left(\pi{r}^{2}\right)}{l}$

For percentage error, we can write $\dfrac{\Deltaρ}{ρ} = \dfrac{\DeltaR}{R} + 2\dfrac{\Deltar}{r} + \dfrac{\Deltal}{l}$

$\dfrac{\Deltaρ}{ρ} \times 100 = \dfrac{\DeltaR}{R} \times 100 + 2\dfrac{\Deltar}{r} \times 100 + \dfrac{\Deltal}{l} \times 100$

$= \left(\dfrac{10}{100} + 2 \times \dfrac{0 .05}{0 .35} + \dfrac{0 .2}{15}\right) \times 100$

$= \left(\dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{2}{7} + \dfrac{1}{75}\right) \times 100$

Hence, $\dfrac{\Deltaρ}{ρ} = 39 .9 %$

$dR = 36\left(\dfrac{0 . 5}{100} + \dfrac{0 . 5}{15 \times 15}\right) = 0 . 26$

$⇒ R = 6 \pm 0 . 26$

$\dfrac{dR}{R} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 26}{6} \times 100$= 4 . 33 %$

questions.q: In an experiment of measuring the refractive index of a glass slab using travelling microscope in physics lab, a student measures real thickness of the glass slab as $5 . 25mm$ and apparent thickness of the glass slab at $5 . 00mm$. Travelling microscope has $20$ divisions in one $cm$ on main scale and $50$ divisions on Vernier scale is equal to $49$ divisions on main scale. The estimated uncertainty in the measurement of refractive index of the slab is $\dfrac{x}{10} \times {10}^{- 3}$, where $x$ is ______
questions.solution:
Given:

$50VSD = 49MSD ⇒ 1VSD = \dfrac{49}{50}MSD$

So least count will be

$= 1MSD - 1VSD = \dfrac{1}{20}cm - \dfrac{49}{50} \cdot \dfrac{1}{20}cm$

$= \dfrac{1}{50} \times \dfrac{1}{20}cm = 0 . 01mm$

As we know, $\mu = \dfrac{h}{h '} = \dfrac{5 . 25}{5 . 00}$

Applying log on both sides, we get

$ln\mu = lnh – lnh ’$

Differentiating both sides, we get

$\dfrac{d\mu}{\mu} = \dfrac{dh}{h} - \dfrac{dh '}{h '}$

For calculation, all errors will be added, therefore

$d\mu = \left[\dfrac{0 . 01}{5 . 25} + \dfrac{0 . 01}{5 . 00}\right]\mu$

$= \dfrac{41}{10} \times {10}^{- 3}$

Hence, $x = 41$

questions.q: In an octagon $ABCDEFGH$ of equal side, what is the sum of $\overset{\to}{AB} + \overset{\to}{AC} + \overset{\to}{AD} + \overset{\to}{AE} + \overset{\to}{AF} + \overset{\to}{AG} + \overset{\to}{AH},$ if, $\overset{\to}{AO} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$
questions.solution:
We know,

$∵ \overset{\to}{OA} + \overset{\to}{OB} + \overset{\to}{OC} + \overset{\to}{OD} + \overset{\to}{OE} + \overset{\to}{OF} + \overset{\to}{OG} + \overset{\to}{OH} = \overset{\to}{0}$

By triangle law of vector addition, we can write

$\overset{\to}{AB} = \overset{\to}{AO} + \overset{\to}{OB}; \overset{\to}{AC} = \overset{\to}{AO} + \overset{\to}{OC}$

$\overset{\to}{AD} = \overset{\to}{AO} + \overset{\to}{OD}; \overset{\to}{AE} = \overset{\to}{AO} + \overset{\to}{OE}$

$\overset{\to}{AF} = \overset{\to}{AO} + \overset{\to}{OF}; \overset{\to}{AG} = \overset{\to}{AO} + \overset{\to}{OG}$

$\overset{\to}{AH} = \overset{\to}{AO} + \overset{\to}{OH}$

Now

$\overset{\to}{AB} + \overset{\to}{AC} + \overset{\to}{AD} + \overset{\to}{AE} + \overset{\to}{AF} + \overset{\to}{AG} + \overset{\to}{AH}$

$= \left(7\overset{\to}{AO}\right) + \overset{\to}{OB} + \overset{\to}{OC} + \overset{\to}{OD} + \overset{\to}{OE} + \overset{\to}{OF} + \overset{\to}{OG} + \overset{\to}{OH}$

$= \left(7\overset{\to}{AO}\right) + \overset{\to}{0} - \overset{\to}{OA}$

$= \left(7\overset{\to}{AO}\right) + \overset{\to}{AO}$

$= 8\overset{\to}{AO} = 8\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= 16\overset{^}{i} + 24\overset{^}{j} - 32\overset{^}{k}$

questions.q: Two vectors $\overset{\to}{A}$ and $\overset{\to}{B}$ have equal magnitudes. The magnitude of $\left(\overset{\to}{A} + \overset{\to}{B}\right)$ is ' $n$ ' times the magnitude of $\left(\overset{\to}{A} - \overset{\to}{B}\right)$ . The angle between $\overset{\to}{A} and \overset{\to}{B}$ is:
questions.solution:
Given: $\left|\overset{\to}{A} + \overset{\to}{B}\right| = n\left|\overset{\to}{A} - \overset{\to}{B}\right|$, so, the magnitudes of this will be given as,

$\sqrt{{A}^{2} + {B}^{2} + 2ABcos\theta} = n\left(\sqrt{{A}^{2} + {B}^{2} - 2ABcos\theta}\right)$;where $\theta$ is the angle between $\overset{\to}{A}$ and $\overset{\to}{B}$.

$\sqrt{2{A}^{2} + 2{A}^{2}cos\theta} = n\sqrt{2{A}^{2} - 2{A}^{2}cos\theta}$

Squaring both sides:

$2{A}^{2}\left(1 + cos\theta\right) = {n}^{2}2{A}^{2}\left(1 - cos\theta\right)$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{{n}^{2} - 1}{{n}^{2} + 1}$

i.e., $\theta = \cos^{- 1}\left[\dfrac{{n}^{2} - 1}{{n}^{2} + 1}\right]$

questions.q: A thin $1m$ long rod has a radius of $5mm$. A force of $50{\text{\pi \times 10}}^{3}N$ is applied at one end to determine its Young's modulus. Assume that the force is exactly known. If the least count in the measurement of all lengths is $0 . 01mm$, which of the following statements is false?
options: The maximum value of $Y$ that can be determined is $2 \times {10}^{14}N{m}^{- 2}$
$\dfrac{∆ Y}{Y}$ gets minimum contribution from the uncertainty in the length.
$\dfrac{∆ Y}{Y}$ gets its maximum contribution from the uncertainty in strain.
The figure of merit is the largest for the length of the rod.
questions.solution:
Given, $l = 1m$, $r = 5 \times 1{0}^{- 3}m$ and $F = 50\text{\pi} \times 1{0}^{3}\text{N}$.

Least count in length is $= 0 . 01mm = 0.01 \times {10}^{- 3}m$
Young's modulus is given by $Y = \dfrac{\dfrac{F}{A}}{\dfrac{∆ l}{l}}$
For, $∆ l \to Min$, $Y \to Max$
$⇒ Y\dfrac{\Delta l}{l} = \dfrac{F}{A}$
$Y = \dfrac{50\text{\pi} \times 1{0}^{3}}{\text{\pi} \times {\left(5 \times 1{0}^{- 3}\right)}^{2}} \times \dfrac{l}{\Delta l}$
$Y = \dfrac{50 \times 1{0}^{3}}{25 \times 1{0}^{- 6}} \times \dfrac{1}{\Delta l} ⇒ Y = \dfrac{2 \times 1{0}^{9}}{\Delta l}$
Here $\Delta l$ is unknown so we can not find the $Y$

The change in young’s modulus ratio is $\dfrac{∆ Y}{Y} = 2\dfrac{∆ r}{r} + \dfrac{∆ l}{l}$.

As seen from above, the minimum contribution to change in young’s modulus is given by the uncertainty in the length and the maximum contributing to the uncertainty in young’s modulus is given by uncertainty in radius.

Hence, correct option is $A$.

questions.q: A vector $\overset{\to}{A}$ is rotated by a small angle $∆ \theta$ radians $\left(∆ \theta ≪ 1\right)$ to get a new vector $\overset{\to}{B}$ . In that case $\left|\overset{\to}{B} - \overset{\to}{A}\right|$ is :
questions.solution:
$\left|\overset{\to}{B}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|$

$\left|\overset{\to}{B} - \overset{\to}{A}\right| = \sqrt{{\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|}^{2} + 2\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|cos\left(180 ° - ∆ \theta\right)}$

$= \sqrt{{\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|}^{2} - 2{\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|}^{2}cos ∆ \theta}$

$= \sqrt{2{\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|}^{2} - 2{\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|}^{2}cos ∆ \theta}$

$= \sqrt{2{\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|}^{2}\left(1 - cos ∆ \theta\right)}$

$∵ 1 - cos ∆ \theta = 2\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{∆ \theta}{2}\right)$

$= \sqrt{2{\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|}^{2} \times 2\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{∆ \theta}{2}\right)}$

$= 2\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|sin\left(\dfrac{∆ \theta}{2}\right)$

For small $∆ \theta, sin\left(\dfrac{∆ \theta}{2}\right) ≃ \left(\dfrac{∆ \theta}{2}\right)$

$\left|\overset{\to}{B} - \overset{\to}{A}\right| = 2\left|\overset{\to}{A}\right|\left(\dfrac{∆ \theta}{2}\right)$

Differentiating

Note: In this method, the $\%$ error obtained is an approximate value on the higher side. Exact value is less than the obtained one.
